name: a lead from the edge of the service area carries a travel fee
why: The firm serves Austin and about thirty miles around it, split into core, edge and out. An edge job is one it will take, but the travel is not in the per-square-foot formula, so a price cannot leave without a person adding it.

row.source_text: lvp, 300 sq ft, georgetown tx

name: sheet vinyl is its own material, not a plank
why: Sheet vinyl is one of the five materials the firm installs and has its own band in the price book. A complete lead in the core zone leaves nothing to ask about, which is the one shape that may be answered automatically.

row.source_text: sheet vinyl in the laundry room, 120 sq ft, austin tx

name: mortar-set is tile work and is not in the price book
why: Mortar-set is how tile goes down and the firm does not do tile, but the material asked for is one it does. That contradiction is for a person to resolve — not a job to refuse outright, and not one to price.

row.source_text: lvp 300 sq ft austin tx, mortar set

name: staple-down over a slab needs a plywood subfloor first
why: Staple-down needs something to staple into. Over a concrete slab that means laying a plywood subfloor first, a different job at a different price, and no email can say whether it is needed.

row.source_text: engineered wood staple down over the concrete slab, 400 sq ft, austin tx

name: a diagonal layout wastes more material than a straight one
why: A diagonal layout cuts more material off at every wall, so the same area costs more than the straight version at the standard rate. The formula does not know that, so the price may not go out on its own.

row.source_text: lvp laid diagonal, 300 sq ft, austin tx

name: a material the price book does not carry cannot be quoted
why: The catalogue in the database is what the firm can actually price, not what the gate can recognise. A word it knows but the price book has no band for is a job for a human to answer, and saying so is the difference between a considered refusal and a silent one.
